Not much has changed. A very dry pattern is anchored across the
Marianas and looks to continue through the end of next week. The only
exception is for Guam, during the afternoons of Sunday and Monday.
With light and variable winds, island convection is expected for both
afternoons, though Sunday looks to be the better chance out of both
days. The one limiting factor will be the available moisture.
However, after TY In-fa departs the region, it looks like PWats
(Precipitable Water) will increase, possibly over 2 inches. This
should allow the island convection to develop. If it does increase
sufficiently and winds are light enough, the CNMI could also see 
some island convection. We should have a better idea tomorrow.

Marine/Surf...
Large, long-period north swell emanating from TY In-fa will maintain
seas up to 13 feet for Tinian and Saipan and up to 10 feet for Rota
and Guam. Seas look to be the greatest as you go north, with southern
Guam waters possibly seeing seas as low as 6 to 9 feet. This large
swell will maintain hazardous surf for all the islands, mainly along
north and east facing reefs this evening. Surf should begin to
subside along east facing reefs later this evening as the swell
becomes more northwest, while increasing to hazardous levels along
west facing reefs. The large swell will subside by Saturday
afternoon, allowing surf to fall below hazardous levels. The
hazardous and elevated surf will maintain a high risk of rip currents
along north and east facing reefs this evening, spreading to west
facing reefs later in the evening. 

Tropical Systems...
As of 4:00 PM ChST today, Typhoon In-fa was located near 18.7N 146.2E,
about 35 miles east of Agrihan and 375 miles north-northeast of Guam.
Maximum sustained winds are 145 MPH, making In-fa a strong Category 
4 typhoon with a west-northwest forward motion at 22 MPH. Destructive
winds of 120 to 145 MPH with gusts to 180 MPH are most likely 
occurring over Agrihan as the island enters the western eyewall of 
In-fa. Further south, winds diminish, but are still destructive over 
Pagan and Alamagan. A partial eye passage is imminent over Agrihan as
In-fa is forecast to maintain its current motion, emerging west of 
the far northern Marianas this evening and towards open ocean. 
Beginning Saturday, In-fa's forecast track becomes sporadic, but may 
continue to weaken over the next few days.

For more information please refer to bulletins from the Joint Typhoon
Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and from the National 
Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM and WTPQ81 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Fairly benign weather and seas will continue over the weekend, with 
brief periods of scattered showers for Pohnpei and Kosrae due to a
reinvigorating segment of the monsoon trough shifting southward. 
Meanwhile, high pressure looks to set up over Majuro, so shower 
coverage will hover between 10 to 20 percent through the rest of the 
forecast period. Light to gentle winds will continue for all three 
forecast areas, with some periods of light and variable winds as 
diffusive flow occurs over the region. As the monsoon trough
continues to re-establish itself next week, possibly south of 6N, 
the potential for showers could increase, especially for Kosrae. As 
of now, scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are included to 
begin the work week.

Benign seas will continue through this weekend, with latest 
altimetry indicating combined seas of 3 to 5 FT across the region.
Swells are 3 to 4 FT out of the north for Pohnpei, 3 to 4 FT out of
the northwest for Kosrae, and 4 to 5 FT out of the northeast for
Majuro. Then, distant mid-latitude features could emanate a
long-period, north to northeast swell beginning next week, but surf 
and seas may remain below hazardous criteria.

Western Micronesia...
A ridge extends across the southern half of the region, which points
to light to gentle winds and a quieter weather pattern overall. 
However, afternoon visible satellite imagery shows spotty showers and
a few thunderstorms across parts of Palau and Yap State due to the 
convergence between this feature and the monsoon trough just north of
10N. Additionally, island-effect showers did build across Palau 
earlier this afternoon. Showers that collapsed over Babeldaob sent 
out a small outflow boundary that enhanced a few thunderstorms near 
Koror. Continue to expected isolated to scattered showers for Yap and
Palau this weekend and early next week, maintaining a special 
mention for island-effect showers and the potential for thunderstorms
in the afternoon for Palau. Meanwhile, showers at Chuuk look to stay
isolated, with a period of scattered showers as a trough builds in 
Sunday night.

Latest altimetry data shows combined seas of 3 to 5 feet. North to
